title: Coordinate of a scaled row projection
statement:
Let $k,d$ be natural numbers, let $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $i$ be a row index in $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$. For every real array $\omega=(\omega_{ij})$, the $i$th coordinate of the image of $x$ under the matrix with entries $\omega_{ij}/\sqrt{k}$ is
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\frac{x_j}{\sqrt{k}}\,\omega_{ij}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $i$ is a row index among the $k$ rows
replaced:
Fix natural numbers $k, d$, a vector $x \in \bbr^d$, and a row index $i \in
\{1,\dots,k\}$. For a sample $\omega$ in the Rademacher sample space
$\mathrm{Rad\Omega}(k,d)$, let $A(\omega)$ be the Rademacher matrix with entries
$\omega_{ij}/\sqrt{k}$. Then, as functions of $\omega$, the $i$-th coordinate of the
image $A(\omega)x$ equals the sum of the scaled entries:
\[
\bigl(A(\omega)\,x\bigr)_i = \sum_{j} \frac{x_j}{\sqrt{k}}\,\omega_{ij}.
\]
